title: MICROSOFT_2023_10K.pdf
summary: This section of Microsoft's Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2023, provides a comprehensive overview of the company's business operations, financial performance, and governance. It includes details on Microsoft's mission, product offerings, risk factors, executive leadership, and internal controls. The financial statements reveal significant revenue growth, particularly in cloud services, while also addressing market risks and legal proceedings. Additionally, it covers executive compensation, stock ownership, and auditor relationships, ensuring transparency and compliance with regulatory requirements.

children.title: Microsoft Form 10-K Front Matter Overview
children.summary: This section contains the front matter of Microsoft's Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2023. It includes essential company information such as the SEC filing type, company address, and registration details for securities. The document confirms Microsoft's status as a large accelerated filer and outlines compliance with reporting requirements. Additionally, it incorporates by reference portions of the definitive Proxy Statement for the upcoming Annual Meeting of Shareholders. The section also includes a note about forward-looking statements, highlighting the nature of projections and associated risks.

children.title: Item 1. Business
children.summary: This section outlines Microsoft's business operations, emphasizing its mission to empower individuals and organizations through technology, particularly AI. It details the company's offerings, including cloud services, productivity tools like Microsoft 365, and gaming through Xbox. The section also highlights Microsoft's commitment to sustainability, diversity, and inclusion, as well as its initiatives to address racial injustice and invest in digital skills. Additionally, it discusses the company's human capital resources, focusing on employee well-being, learning opportunities, and pay equity, while providing an overview of its operating segments.

children.title: Information about our Executive Officers
children.summary: This section provides detailed information about Microsoft's executive officers as of July 27, 2023, including their names, ages, and positions within the company. Key executives highlighted include Satya Nadella, the Chairman and CEO, and other senior leaders such as Judson B. Althoff, Chief Commercial Officer, and Amy E. Hood, Chief Financial Officer. The section outlines their career trajectories within Microsoft and previous roles, showcasing their experience and contributions to the company. This information is relevant for understanding the leadership structure and expertise driving Microsoft's strategic direction.

children.title: Item 1A. Risk Factors
children.summary: This section outlines various risk factors that could negatively impact the company's operations and financial performance. Key risks include intense competition in technology and platform ecosystems, which may lead to reduced revenue and operating margins. The company faces challenges from competitors utilizing different business models, including free applications and open-source software. Additionally, significant investments in new technologies, such as AI, may not yield expected returns. Cybersecurity threats and data privacy issues are also highlighted, emphasizing the potential for reputational damage and financial loss due to breaches or misuse of customer data. Overall, the section serves to inform stakeholders of the uncertainties and challenges the company may encounter in its business environment.

children.title: Item 1B. Unresolved Staff Comments
children.summary: This section confirms that there are no unresolved written comments from the Securities and Exchange Commission regarding the company's periodic or current reports that were issued 180 days or more before the end of fiscal year 2023. It indicates compliance with regulatory requirements and suggests that the company has effectively addressed any prior inquiries from the SEC. Readers can learn about the company's standing with regulatory bodies and its transparency in reporting.

children.title: Item 2. Properties
children.summary: This section details the company's properties, including its corporate headquarters in Redmond, Washington, which encompasses approximately 16 million square feet of space for various operational purposes. It specifies that about 11 million square feet are owned and 5 million square feet are leased, with additional facilities located both domestically and internationally for offices, datacenters, and research and development. Key international locations include China, India, Ireland, and the Netherlands for owned properties, and Australia, Canada, and several European countries for leased properties. The company has also made strategic decisions to consolidate office leases to optimize workspace density, indicating ongoing evaluations of real estate needs.

children.title: Item 3. Legal Proceedings
children.summary: This section references Note 15 – Contingencies in the Notes to Financial Statements for details on ongoing legal proceedings involving the company. It indicates that there are legal matters that may impact the company's financial position or operations, but does not provide specific details within this section itself. Readers can learn about the nature and status of these legal proceedings by consulting the referenced note.

children.title: Item 4. Mine Safety Disclosures
children.summary: This section, Item 4, Mine Safety Disclosures, states that it is not applicable to the company. It indicates that there are no relevant mine safety disclosures to report, suggesting that the company does not operate in mining or related industries that would require such disclosures. Readers can learn that the company is not subject to mine safety regulations or reporting requirements.

children.title: Item 5. Market for Registrant’s Common Equity, Related Stockholder Matters, and Issuer Purchases of Equity Securities
children.summary: This section provides an overview of the market for the registrant's common equity, specifically focusing on its trading status on the NASDAQ under the symbol MSFT and the number of registered stockholders as of July 24, 2023. It details the monthly share repurchases for the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2023, including the total number of shares purchased, average price paid, and the remaining dollar value available for repurchase under announced plans. Additionally, it outlines dividends declared during the same period, including declaration, record, and payment dates, as well as the amount per share. The total return to shareholders through repurchases and dividends for the quarter is reported as $9.7 billion, with a reference to further details in the financial statements.

children.title: Item 6. [Reserved]
children.summary: This section is reserved and does not contain any content or information. It serves as a placeholder for potential future use or additional information that may be added later. Readers will not find any specific topics, facts, or details in this section as it is intentionally left blank.

children.title: Item 7. Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations
children.summary: This section provides an analysis of Microsoft's financial condition and operational results for the fiscal year ending June 30, 2023, compared to the previous year. Key highlights include a 22% increase in Microsoft Cloud revenue, driven by Azure and Office 365 growth, while Windows OEM and Devices revenues saw significant declines. The discussion also addresses economic conditions, competitive challenges, and strategic investments in AI and cloud infrastructure. Additionally, it outlines changes in accounting estimates affecting operating income and net income, and provides insights into segment performance, operating expenses, and tax rates.

children.title: Item 7A. Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures about Market Risk
children.summary: This section discusses the company's exposure to various market risks, including foreign exchange rates, interest rates, credit risk, and equity prices. It details the use of derivative instruments to manage these risks and highlights specific currency exposures such as the Euro and Japanese yen. The section also includes a sensitivity analysis that quantifies potential losses in earnings and fair values due to hypothetical changes in market conditions, such as a 10% decrease in foreign exchange rates or a 100 basis point increase in interest rates. Overall, it provides insights into the company's risk management strategies and the financial impact of market fluctuations.

children.title: Item 8. Financial Statements and Supplementary Data
children.summary: This section provides a comprehensive overview of Microsoft's financial statements for the fiscal year ending June 30, 2023, including income statements, balance sheets, cash flow statements, and stockholders' equity statements. Key financial metrics such as total revenue, net income, and earnings per share are detailed, showing a total revenue of $211.9 billion and net income of $72.4 billion. The section also discusses comprehensive income, detailing other comprehensive losses and adjustments. Additionally, it outlines significant accounting policies, revenue recognition practices, and the impact of estimates and assumptions on financial reporting, providing insights into the company's financial health and operational performance.

children.title: Item 9. Changes in and Disagreements with Accountants on Accounting and Financial Disclosure
children.summary: This section indicates that there were no changes or disagreements with accountants regarding accounting and financial disclosure. It details the evaluation of the effectiveness of the company's disclosure controls and procedures, confirming their effectiveness as of the reporting period's end. Management is responsible for maintaining adequate internal control over financial reporting, which is designed to ensure the reliability of financial reporting in accordance with U.S. GAAP. The section also notes that an evaluation based on the COSO framework concluded that internal controls were effective as of June 30, 2023, with no material changes affecting these controls during the quarter. Additionally, it mentions that Deloitte & Touche LLP audited the internal controls, and their report is included in the document.

children.title: Item 9A. Controls and Procedures
children.summary: This section discusses the evaluation of the company's disclosure controls and procedures, confirming their effectiveness as of the reporting period's end. It outlines management's responsibility for maintaining adequate internal control over financial reporting, which aims to ensure the reliability of financial statements in accordance with U.S. GAAP. The evaluation was based on the Internal Control – Integrated Framework (2013) by COSO, concluding that internal controls were effective as of June 30, 2023, with no significant changes reported during the quarter. Additionally, it mentions that Deloitte & Touche LLP audited these controls, with their report included in this item.

children.title: Report of Management on Internal Control over Financial Reporting
children.summary: This section outlines the management's responsibility for establishing and maintaining effective internal control over financial reporting. It describes the process aimed at ensuring the reliability of financial reporting in accordance with U.S. GAAP, including maintaining accurate records and preventing unauthorized asset transactions. Management evaluated the effectiveness of these controls using the COSO framework and concluded that they were effective as of June 30, 2023. Additionally, it notes that there were no significant changes to the internal controls during the reporting period, and mentions that Deloitte & Touche LLP conducted an audit of these controls.

children.title: Report of Independent Registered Public Accounting Firm
children.summary: This section contains the report from Deloitte & Touche LLP, the independent registered public accounting firm, regarding Microsoft Corporation's internal control over financial reporting as of June 30, 2023. The firm expresses an unqualified opinion that Microsoft maintained effective internal control in all material respects, based on the COSO framework. The report outlines the responsibilities of both the company's management and the auditors, detailing the audit process and the inherent limitations of internal controls. It emphasizes the importance of internal controls in ensuring reliable financial reporting and compliance with generally accepted accounting principles.

children.title: Item 9B. Other Information
children.summary: This section reports that during the three months ending June 30, 2023, no directors or officers disclosed the adoption or termination of any trading arrangements as defined by SEC rules. It also states that there are no applicable disclosures regarding foreign jurisdictions that prevent inspections. The section serves to inform stakeholders about compliance with trading regulations and the absence of relevant changes in trading arrangements among executives.

children.title: Item 9C. Disclosure Regarding Foreign Jurisdictions that Prevent Inspections
children.summary: Item 9C states that the disclosure regarding foreign jurisdictions that prevent inspections is not applicable. This indicates that there are no foreign jurisdictions affecting the company's ability to conduct inspections as per regulatory requirements. Readers can learn that the company is not currently facing any barriers related to foreign inspections, which may impact transparency and compliance.

children.title: Item 10. Directors, Executive Officers, and Corporate Governance
children.summary: This section provides an overview of the company's directors and executive officers, directing readers to the Proxy Statement for detailed biographical information and governance practices. It mentions the adoption of the Microsoft Finance Code of Professional Conduct, which applies to key financial executives, and outlines the process for disclosing any amendments or waivers to this code. Additionally, it references the incorporation of information regarding director nominees, audit committee details, and executive compensation from the Proxy Statement, ensuring transparency in corporate governance.

children.title: Item 11. Executive Compensation
children.summary: This section references the Proxy Statement for detailed information on executive compensation, including director compensation, named executive officer compensation, and the Compensation Committee's report. It also mentions the potential inclusion of details regarding compensation committee interlocks and insider participation, if applicable. Readers can find specific compensation figures and policies related to executive pay by consulting the referenced Proxy Statement.

children.title: Item 12. Security Ownership of Certain Beneficial Owners and Management and Related Stockholder Matters
children.summary: This section provides information on the security ownership of certain beneficial owners and management, referencing details found in the Proxy Statement under 'Stock Ownership Information,' 'Principal Shareholders,' and 'Equity Compensation Plan Information.' It highlights the ownership stakes of key stakeholders, including directors and executive officers, and outlines the equity compensation plans in place. Readers can learn about the distribution of shares among management and significant shareholders, which is crucial for understanding potential influences on corporate governance and decision-making.

children.title: Item 13. Certain Relationships and Related Transactions, and Director Independence
children.summary: This section references the Proxy Statement for details on director independence and certain relationships and related transactions. It indicates that the guidelines for director independence and any relevant transactions involving directors are incorporated by reference from the Proxy Statement. Readers can learn about the criteria used to assess director independence and any potential conflicts of interest related to transactions with directors.

children.title: Item 14. Principal Accountant Fees and Services
children.summary: This section provides details about the fees and services rendered by the principal accountant, Deloitte & Touche LLP, including the specific amounts billed for audit and non-audit services. It references the Proxy Statement for comprehensive information under the headings 'Fees Billed by Deloitte & Touche' and 'Policy on Audit Committee Pre-Approval of Audit and Permissible Non-Audit Services of Independent Auditor.' Readers can learn about the financial relationship between the company and its auditor, as well as the governance policies regarding auditor services.

children.title: Item 15. Exhibit and Financial Statement Schedules
children.summary: This section provides an overview of the financial statements and schedules for Microsoft Corporation, detailing their location within the Form 10-K. It includes an index to key financial documents such as income statements, balance sheets, and cash flow statements. Additionally, it lists various exhibits, including articles of incorporation, bylaws, indentures, and stock plans, along with their filing dates and forms. The section serves to inform stakeholders about the financial reporting and governance documents relevant to the company.

children.title: Item 16. Form 10-K Summary
children.summary: This section indicates that there is no summary provided for Item 16 of the Form 10-K. It suggests that the company has chosen not to include any additional information or highlights in this part of the report. Readers will find that there are no key topics, facts, or insights available in this section.

children.title: Signatures
children.summary: This section includes the signatures of key executives and directors of Microsoft Corporation, affirming the authenticity of the report filed under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934. It features signatures from the Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer, and various directors, indicating their approval and responsibility for the report's contents. Additionally, it contains certifications from Satya Nadella and Amy E. Hood, confirming compliance with financial reporting requirements and the accuracy of the financial statements. The section serves to validate the report and ensure accountability among the company's leadership.
